title: We Are Born Good Wins Best Film at Taiwan's 2026 Golden Horse Awards
excerpt:
Hong Kong drama We Are Born Good claimed Best Film and Original Screenplay at the Golden Horse Awards.
Double Happiness and The Violinist were among the night's other major winners.
body_md:
Hong Kong drama We Are Born Good, written and directed by Yeung Leung-chuen, emerged as a major winner at Taiwan's Golden Horse Awards, taking Best Film and Best Original Screenplay. The film previously premiered in the Discovery program at the Toronto International Film Festival, and Edko Films is handling international sales.

The story begins with an incident involving two people at a restaurant. What initially appears to be a minor mishap escalates into a serious feud, providing the basis for a drama about conflict and the consequences of an increasingly hostile relationship. The awards report does not establish a general theatrical release date or offer enough detail to draw conclusions about the characters' eventual fates.

Double Happiness, a Taiwanese comedy-drama directed by Joseph Hsu Chen-chieh, was another prominent title. Its prospective groom must organize two separate weddings on the same day for his divorced parents without either discovering the arrangement. Liu Kuan-ting won Best Leading Actor, while the film also collected Best Film Editing and the Audience Choice Award. The report's narrative describes a Best Director win for the film, but its published winners list names Herman Yau for that category. That discrepancy should not be overlooked or treated as resolved.

Angela Yuen received Best Leading Actress for Afterpiece, directed by Keane T.K. Wong and produced by Derek Yee. She plays an aspiring actress chosen for a significant part by a filmmaker attempting a comeback. Anson Kong Ip-sang, who is also a member of the Hong Kong boy band Mirror, won Best Supporting Actor for Herman Yau's social drama We're Nothing At All. Judy Ongg was named Best Supporting Actress for Sunshine Women's Choir, a box-office success in Taiwan.

The Violinist, an animated feature by Ervin Han and Raul Garcia, won both Best Animated Feature and Best Adapted Screenplay. Shu Qi's Girl earned Best New Director as well as the FIPRESCI critics' prize. Among technical winners, Giddens Ko's Kung Fu received awards for visual effects, makeup and costume design, and action choreography. Malaysian drama Dead Tide was recognized for cinematography and original film song.

The Golden Horse Awards remain among the most prominent honors for Chinese-language cinema. This year's ceremony was held at Taipei Music Center on November 22, concluding the Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival, which ran from November 6 through November 22, 2026. Mainland China has boycotted the awards since 2019 following a political statement by an award recipient, a continuing part of the event's broader context.

The range of recognized productions illustrates the variety of filmmaking represented at the ceremony, from intimate dramas and social stories to animation and technically ambitious genre work. Awards recognition can bring greater visibility, but it does not in itself establish a film's future international distribution or commercial performance.
